description:
We're building a web game where players design a space mission (rocket, payload, trajectory) under real constraints like budget, fuel, and launch windows, then watch it play out in 3D using real NASA data.

Looking for: React/frontend dev, Three.js/3D dev, Python backend dev, NASA data researcher, UI/UX designer, and a pitch/video maker.
summary:
Stellavex is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform developed to make the complexities of space exploration more accessible and engaging. It allows users to experience the role of mission designers by configuring spacecraft, selecting scientific payloads, managing limited resources, and making critical operational decisions.
Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python, with FastAPI powering its backend, Stellavex combines an interactive frontend with a simulation engine that evaluates mission configurations and outcomes.

The project addresses the challenge of planning successful space missions under technical constraints and limited resources. It incorporates five essential resources: power, budget, data, communications, and time. Users must balance these interconnected requirements while considering how their engineering choices affect overall mission performance. Through mission simulations, they can evaluate different configurations, and understand the factors influencing mission success.

Stellavex is important because it bridges the gap between theoretical space science and practical learning. By transforming complex aerospace concepts into an interactive experience, it promotes scientific curiosity, engineering awareness, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Ultimately, its goal is to make space exploration more understandable and inspire students to engage with the science and technology shaping humanity's future beyond Earth.
details:
Stellavex – Interactive Space Mission Design and Simulation Platform

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o-7nts6ICFI

Stellavex is an interactive, web-based space mission design and simulation platform developed to explore the complexities of spacecraft engineering, mission planning, and resource management. It places users in the role of space mission designers, challenging them to develop spacecraft configurations capable of achieving scientific objectives while operating within technical, financial, and resource constraints.

The platform transforms the traditionally complex process of space mission planning into an accessible, interactive experience. Users can customize spacecraft by selecting different components, including propulsion systems, power sources, payloads, communication systems, and scientific instruments. Each selection influences the mission's capabilities and resource requirements. Users must strategically balance factors such as spacecraft performance, available power, budget, data generation, communication capacity, and mission duration to create a viable mission design.

Beyond spacecraft configuration, Stellavex incorporates an interactive mission simulation system that evaluates proposed designs and introduces in-flight decisions. This allows users to experience how initial engineering choices and operational decisions can affect mission performance. The platform also incorporates mission scoring and leaderboard functionality, encouraging experimentation, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.

Technical Implementation and Development

Stellavex was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for its frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering its backend architecture. JavaScript handles the interactive game environment and mission logic, while the Python backend manages API communication and simulation-related operations. The application includes dedicated endpoints for mission simulation, spacecraft catalog retrieval, score submission, leaderboard data, and mission statistics.

An important technical aspect is its server-side score verification mechanism. Submitted mission results are independently validated by rerunning the simulation using the original spacecraft design, seed, and in-flight decisions. This improves the reliability and integrity of the scoring system rather than relying solely on results reported by the client.

The project was developed as a browser-accessible application, using software-based development and testing processes without requiring specialized physical hardware.

Innovation, Creativity, and Intended Impact

The primary innovation behind Stellavex lies in combining spacecraft engineering principles with interactive simulation and game-based learning. Instead of limiting users to theoretical explanations of space technology, it provides an environment in which they can actively experiment with mission configurations, evaluate trade-offs, and observe the consequences of their decisions.

During development, particular attention was given to resource optimization, engineering feasibility, mission reliability, scientific objectives, simulation consistency, scoring integrity, and user accessibility.

Ultimately, Stellavex aims to promote interest in space exploration, make aerospace engineering concepts more approachable, and encourage the next generation to engage with science, technology, engineering, and problem-solving. It demonstrates how interactive digital platforms can transform complex scientific concepts into practical, engaging learning experiences.
